question.problem: What is $\frac{yz}{3xz}$ reduced to lowest terms?
question.worked_solution:
First, we decompose all of the terms into their various factors.

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{yz}{3xz}=\frac{y\cdot z}{3\cdot x\cdot z}\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we cancel out all the pairs of common factors in the numerator and denominator. In this case, there is one pair of $z$'s.

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{y\cdot z}{3\cdot x\cdot z} & = \\ \frac{y\cdot \cancel{z}}{3\cdot x\cdot \cancel{z}} & = \\ \frac{y}{3x}\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, the expression simplifies to $\frac{y}{3x}.$
